It is in the singular, construed according to the form of «مَنْ», just as «هُوَ» is singular; and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَما مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ) The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is negative; «مِنَّا» is a fronted khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its qualifier having taken its place, the implied form being "and none of us is there but has a known station", as in the poet's words:
أنا ابن جلا وطلاع الثنايا ... متى أضع العمامة تعرفوني
(I am the son of one who disclosed matters and who climbs the mountain passes; when I take off my turban, you will know me), that is, "I am the son of a man who disclosed matters." It is also permissible that «مِنَّا» be a qualifier of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the khabar be the clause «إِلَّا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ»; «إِلَّا» is a particle of restriction; «لَهُ» is a fronted khabar, «مَقامٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ and «مَعْلُومٌ» an adjective. The wording of al-Qurṭubī: "Allah the Exalted revealed, relating the saying of the angels: «وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم». According to the Kufans the implied form is «وما منا إلا من له مقام معلوم», the relative «من» being omitted; according to the Basrans the implied form is «وما منا ملك إلا له مقام معلوم», that is, a known place in worship."

* Benefits:
The khabar must be omitted when the mubtadaʾ is followed by a noun conjoined to it with a wāw that is explicit in meaning accompaniment, as in «كل رجل وضيعته» ("every man and his livelihood"), «ضيعته» meaning his trade, so called because its owner is lost (yaḍīʿu) in it, and «كل صانع وما صنع» ("every maker and what he made"). Here «كل» is a mubtadaʾ, «صانع» is a muḍāf ilayhi, «وما صنع» is conjoined to the mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is necessarily omitted, the implied form being "paired" (muqtarinān). It is omitted only because the wāw and what follows it indicate companionship and pairing. But when there is no explicit indication of accompaniment, it may be omitted and it may be mentioned. An example of the latter is the verse of al-Farazdaq:
تمنوا لي الموت الذي يشعب الفتى ... وكل امرئ والموت يلتقيان
(They wished for me the death that parts the youth; every man and death will meet), where he preferred to mention the khabar, the clause «يلتقيان». «يشعب» means "separates".

dervis-irab:165-173.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الصَّافُّونَ) The wāw is conjunctive; inna and its noun; the shifted lām; «نَحْنُ» is a mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and «الصَّافُّونَ» is the khabar of «نَحْنُ», the nominal clause being the khabar of «إِنَّا»; or «الصَّافُّونَ» is the khabar of «إِنَّا», meaning "we stand in a single rank in prayer or on the field of jihad". The object of «الصَّافُّونَ» is omitted, that is, "we line up our feet".
(وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْمُسَبِّحُونَ) Conjoined to the preceding verse. (وَإِنْ كانُوا لَيَقُولُونَ لَوْ أَنَّ عِنْدَنا ذِكْراً مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The wāw is conjunctive; «إِنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy «إِنَّ», inoperative; or, if it is made to operate, its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause «كانُوا» is its khabar. «كان» and its noun, and the discriminating lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); the clause «يَقُولُونَ» is the khabar of kāna; the clause «لَوْ» and what follows it is the content of their saying; «لَوْ» is conditional; «أَنَّ» and what follows it is the agent of an omitted verb, that is, "it had been established"; «أَنَّ» is a particle resembling a verb; the adverbial is attached to an omitted element that is the fronted khabar of «أَنَّ», and «ذِكْراً» is its postponed noun; «مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ» is an adjective of «ذِكْراً». (لَكُنَّا عِبادَ اللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ) The lām occurs in the apodosis of «لَوْ»; «كان» and its noun; «عِبادَ اللَّهِ» is its predicate, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «الْمُخْلَصِينَ» is an adjective of «عِبادَ اللَّهِ». (فَكَفَرُوا بِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; «كَفَرُوا» is a past verb and an agent; the fāʾ is conjunctive; «سَوْفَ» is a particle of futurity; «يَعْلَمُونَ» is an imperfect verb in the nominative and an agent.
(وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنا لِعِبادِنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive statement introduced to affirm the threat and depict it with an oath, to emphasise it and show concern for it. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «قَدْ» is a particle of certainty; «سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنا» is a verb and an agent; «لِعِبادِنَا» is attached to «سَبَقَتْ», and «الْمُرْسَلِينَ» is an adjective of «لِعِبادِنَا». (إِنَّهُمْ لَهُمُ الْمَنْصُورُونَ) Inna and its noun; the shifted lām; «هُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun, and «الْمَنْصُورُونَ» is the khabar of «هُمْ», the clause being the khabar of «إِنَّهُمْ»; or it is the khabar of «إِنَّهُمْ» and the separating pronoun has no position. َ إِنَّ جُنْدَنا لَهُمُ الْغالِبُونَ) [Translator's note: the opening of this verse is garbled in the source, which prints it with a stray diacritic and a closing parenthesis only.]
Conjoined to its counterpart mentioned just above.

* Benefits:
A return to the separating pronoun:
The discussion of the separating pronoun has preceded in this book. We add here to what was said that calling it a "pronoun" is figurative, because of the resemblance of its form. The majority of the Basrans agree that it is discarded and has no position, but they nonetheless differ over whether it is a noun or a particle. Most of them said it is a noun that has been discarded, as the nouns of verbs (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) and the relative «ال» were discarded. Some of them said it is a particle, because they found it objectionable that a noun be devoid of i'rab both in form and in position, and because its purpose is to avert confusion of the following khabar with an adjective, and this is the meaning of a particle, namely conveying meaning in something else. So it became a particle and the garment of nounhood was stripped from it, like the kāf of address: when it was stripped of the meaning of nounhood and entered the meaning of a particle, namely conveying meaning in something else. It was also said that it has a position in i'rab, and this is the doctrine of the Kufans, who say that it is tawkīd (emphasis) of what precedes, since a nominative pronoun may be used to emphasise an accusative or genitive one, as in «ضربتك أنت» ("I struck you, you") and «مررت بك أنت» ("I passed by you, you").

dervis-irab:174-182.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِساحَتِهِمْ) : Their courtyard. Al-Farrāʾ said: The Arabs content themselves with mentioning the courtyard for the people. The original meaning of «الساحة» is the courtyard empty of buildings; its plural is «سوح», so its alif is converted from a wāw, and the diminutive is «سويحة»; the plural and the diminutive return things to their origins. Al-Rāghib said that it belongs to the roots ending in yāʾ, since he counted it under the root s-y-ḥ, then he said: "«الساحة» is the wide place, and from it comes the courtyard of the house; «السائح» is water flowing in the courtyard, and «ساح فلان في الأرض» means he passed like the flowing water; and a man is «سائح» and «سياح»." On this view it would have two roots, but al-Rāghib's discussion is deficient. In al-Asās he mentioned it under the root s-w-ḥ, and its wording is: "«عمر الله تعالى بك ساحتك» (may Allah the Exalted make your courtyard flourish through you); and you say «احمرّ اللّوح، واغبرّت السوح» (the sky reddened and the courtyards became dusty) when drought occurs." Abū Dhuʾayb said:
وكان سيان أن لا يسرحوا نعما ... أو يسرحوه بها واغبرت السوح
(It was all the same whether they did not send out livestock or sent it out, while the courtyards turned dusty.) Al-Asās did not mention «الساحة» under the root s-y-ḥ, so they are two roots. In al-Qāmūs he listed «الساحة» among the roots ending in wāw, saying: "«الساحة» is the tract and the open space between the dwellings of the tribe; the plural is «ساح», «سوح» and «ساحات»", and he did not mention it under the root «ساح يسيح سيحا وسيحانا» and so on.

* I'rab:
(فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى حِينٍ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, "if the reality of their affair has become clear to you, then turn away from them". «تَوَلَّ» is an imperative verb indeclinable by deletion of the weak letter, meaning "turn away from them", and the agent is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "you"; «عَنْهُمْ» is attached to «تَوَلَّ»; «حَتَّى» is a particle of limit and genitive; «حِينٍ» is genitive through «حَتَّى», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تَوَلَّ».
(وَأَبْصِرْهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ) The wāw is conjunctive; «أَبْصِرْهُمْ» is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object, meaning "when the punishment descends upon their courtyard". The fāʾ links the apodosis of a command; «سَوْفَ» is a particle of futurity; «يُبْصِرُونَ» is an imperfect verb and an agent, and the direct object is omitted, that is, "what will befall them as requital for their disbelief". (أَفَبِعَذابِنا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ) The hamza is interrogative, and the meaning of the interrogation here is threat and menace; the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted clause that is implied according to the context; «بِعَذابِنا» is attached to «يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ», and «يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is the agent.
(فَإِذا نَزَلَ بِساحَتِهِمْ فَساءَ صَباحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ) The fāʾ is conjunctive; «إِذا» is an adverbial of the future that carries the sense of a condition; «نَزَلَ» is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", that is, the punishment; «بِساحَتِهِمْ» is attached to «نَزَلَ»; the fāʾ links the apodosis of «إِذا»; «ساءَ» is a verb that does not inflect, to express blame; «صَباحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ» is its agent, and the object of the blame is omitted, its implied form being "their morning". It was also said that the pronoun of «ساءَ» refers to the specified object of blame, that the tamyīz is omitted, and that the noun mentioned is the specified object and not the agent; more of this discussion will come.
(وَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى حِينٍ) Conjoined to what has preceded; the i'rab of this repeated verse has already been given. (وَأَبْصِرْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ) Its i'rab has preceded; the object of «أَبْصِرْ» is omitted for brevity because the first indicates it. (سُبْحانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ) «سُبْحانَ رَبِّكَ» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; «رَبِّ الْعِزَّةِ» is a badal; «عَمَّا» is attached to «سُبْحانَ», and the clause «يَصِفُونَ» is the ṣila of «ما». (وَسَلامٌ عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ) «سَلامٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, for which it is acceptable to begin because of the sense of supplication in it, and «عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ» is the khabar. (وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) «الْحَمْدُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «لِلَّهِ» a khabar, and «رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ» is a badal or an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «فإذا نزل بساحتهم فساء صباح المنذرين» there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). The punishment that descends upon them after they were warned of it, yet took no notice of the warning and stopped their ears against it, is likened to an army whose attack one of its well-wishers warned his people of, but they paid no heed to his warning and took no precaution or care, which might have saved them from the terror of the disaster and enabled them to avoid its sudden woes. The morning was singled out only because it was the habit of their raiders and fighters to attack then, so the raid was called "morning" (ṣabāḥ) because it usually occurs in it; for this reason the Arabs deemed this verse most eloquent.

* Benefits:
Every triliteral verb that is inflecting, complete, affirmative, capable of degrees, in the active voice, and whose adjective is not of the pattern «أفعل فعلاء», and from which wonder may be expressed, may be used on the pattern «فعُل» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, either originally, as in «ظرف» and «شرف», or by conversion, in that it was originally with fatḥa on the ʿayn, like «ضرب» and «قتل», or with kasra, like «علم» and «فهم», with ḍamma in them. They were converted only to be joined to the verbs of innate qualities and to become intransitive and non-inflecting. It then follows the course of niʿma and biʾsa in conveying praise and blame, and in the ruling of the agent and the ruling of the specified object. You say in praise «فهم الرجل زيد» and «فهم رجلا زيد», and in blame «خبث الرجل عمرو» and «خبث رجلا عمرو». Among its examples is «ساء», which is originally «سوأ» with fatḥa, from «السوء», the opposite of joy, from «ساءه الأمر يسوءه» when it grieved him; so it was transitive and inflecting, then converted to «فعُل» with ḍamma so it became intransitive, then it was given the meaning of biʾsa, so it became non-inflecting and intransitive, its agent being given the ruling given to the agent of biʾsa. You say «ساء الرجل زيد», and in the Revelation: «وساءت مرتفقا». An example that admits of being an agent or a tamyīz is «ساء ما يحكمون»; its discussion has preceded.

dervis-irab:20-26.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا يا وَيْلَنا هذا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ): The wāw is resumptive; قالوا is a verb and agent; يا is a particle of alerting, or the one addressed is omitted; ويلنا is a verbal noun with no verb of its own wording, or it is the one addressed; the clause of the vocative is the content of their saying. The clause هذا يوم الدين may be part of the rest of their saying, or the pause may be completed at ويلنا and the clause be resumptive, in which case it is from the saying of the angels to them. هذا is the mubtadaʾ and يوم الدين its khabar. (هذا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ): هذا is the mubtadaʾ and يوم الفصل the khabar. The clause may be part of the rest of their saying, in which case the saying «تكذبون» is an iltifāt (shift) from the first person to the second. الذي is an adjective of يوم; كنتم: كان and its noun; به is attached to تكذبون; and the clause تكذبون is the khabar of كنتم.
(احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْواجَهُمْ وَما كانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ): An address from Allah the Exalted to the angels, or from some of them to others. احشروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila, and the relative noun is a designation of the polytheists; the object of ظلموا is omitted, its implied form being "themselves". وأزواجهم is conjoined to the relative noun, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); وما is likewise conjoined, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu; كان and its noun, and the clause يعبدون is its khabar.
(مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلى صِراطِ الْجَحِيمِ): من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the fāʾ is a conjunction; اهدوهم is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; إلى صراط الجحيم is attached to اهدوهم. (وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَسْؤُلُونَ): وقفوهم is conjoined to what precedes, i.e. "and detain them at the Path"; إن and its noun, and مسؤولون is its khabar, the clause being a justification of the command.
(ما لَكُمْ لا تَناصَرُونَ): The clause is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "and it is said, in reproach to them". ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; لكم is the khabar; the clause لا تناصرون is circumstantial; لا is negative; تناصرون is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs was dropped, the original being لا تتناصرون, i.e. you do not help one another. (بَلْ هُمُ الْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ): بل is a particle of rejection and conjunction; هم is the mubtadaʾ; اليوم is an adverb attached to مستسلمون; مستسلمون is the khabar of هم, i.e. some of them have handed over others and abandoned them out of incapacity.

* Benefits:
In the imperfect verb beginning with two additional tāʾs, both assimilation (idghām) and separation are permitted. We cite here a discussion among the scholars of Arabic, of which we give the gist for its usefulness and charm. Ibn Mālik mentioned in Sharḥ al-Kāfiya, and his son followed him in Sharḥ al-Khulāṣa, that if you assimilate the first tāʾ into the second you bring in a hamzat al-waṣl to arrive by it at pronouncing the tāʾ made silent for the assimilation, so you say اتجلى for تتجلى. Ibn Hishām in Awḍaḥ al-Masālik, and Shaykh Khālid al-Azharī following him, rebutted them, saying: "There is something to consider in this, for Allah has not created, so far as we know, any of the eloquent who put a hamzat al-waṣl at the beginning of an imperfect verb; the assimilation of this kind is only in continuous speech, not at the beginning. Al-Ḥawfī said: if one pauses, one begins with the unassimilated form, and it is not permissible to introduce the alif of waṣl, because the alif of waṣl does not enter the imperfect verb. The versifier — i.e. Ibn Mālik — stated this question correctly in some of his books, saying: it is permissible to assimilate the tāʾ of the imperfect into another tāʾ after a lengthening or a vowel, as in ولا تيمموا and تكاد تميز."
Some scholars replied to them, saying: There is something to consider in this criticism, because Ibn Mālik and his son are among the most eminent scholars of Arabic, and they said that assimilation is permissible at the beginning with a hamzat al-waṣl brought in because it is impossible to begin with a silent letter. Their case is one of two things: either they relied on understanding this from the language of the Arabs, or they derived it from it because nothing contradicts or opposes it. In either case it is not good to rebut them merely by the absence of knowledge that Allah did not create a hamzat al-waṣl at the beginning of the imperfect verb, because they are affirming and the one rebutting them is denying, and the affirmer takes precedence over the denier, and one who has memorised is proof against one who has not. Do not suppose that they ventured on what they held merely out of desire, without relying on something they depended on and referred to, for ill opinion of the leading scholars is unbecoming. How could it be, when trustworthy people have reported that Ibn Mālik said: "I studied al-Ṣiḥāḥ and benefited from it only three points"? Their not mentioning the support for this explicitly does no harm to them, even if they mentioned it by allusion. The son of the author said: "Among them are those who assimilate, make the first letter silent, and bring in a hamzat al-waṣl, saying اتجلى" — for the two are trustworthy and reliable. The author of al-Qāmūs mentioned in the section of jīm, chapter of nūn, when speaking of Jayyān: "From it are the two imams of Arabic, Ibn Mālik and Abū Ḥayyān."

dervis-irab:27-34.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ): The wāw is resumptive; أقبل is a past verb; بعضهم is the fāʿil; على بعض is attached to أقبل; and the clause يتساءلون is circumstantial, i.e. they blame one another and some of them direct reproach at others. (قالُوا إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ): قالوا is a verb and agent; ان and its noun, and the clause كنتم is its khabar; كان and its noun, and the clause تأتوننا is its khabar; تأتوننا is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object; عن اليمين is a ḥāl from the agent of تأتونا. As for اليمين, either the limb is meant, expressing by it strength, or the oath, because those who conclude a contract by oath confirm their oath by clasping hands with the right and wiping with it. There are many other sayings that we have passed over, to be consulted in the longer works; the gist of the meaning is: "You deceived us and led us astray." (قالُوا بَلْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ): This is one of the five answers of those who were followed, the first of them, and it is a rejecting rejection (iḍrāb ibṭālī) of what the followers claimed, i.e. you were not characterised by faith at any time. قالوا is a verb and agent; بل is a rejecting rejection; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تكونوا is an imperfect verb made jussive by لم, the wāw its noun, and مؤمنين its khabar.
(وَما كانَ لَنا عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ): This is the second answer, and it is built on the supposition that they led them astray, whereas they did not force them to it. ما is negative; كان is an incomplete past verb; لنا is its predicate put forward; عليكم is a ḥāl; من is a redundant preposition; and سلطان is genitive in form, but the noun of كان in position. (بَلْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْماً طاغِينَ): بل is also a rejecting rejection; كنتم: كان and its noun; قوما its khabar; طاغين an adjective of قوما; and this is the third answer. (فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنا قَوْلُ رَبِّنا إِنَّا لَذائِقُونَ): This is the fourth answer. The fāʾ is a conjunction; حق is a past verb; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حق; قول ربنا is the fāʿil; ان and its noun, the shifted lām, and ذائقون is its khabar; the nominal clause is a justification of what precedes; the object of ذائقون is omitted, i.e. "the punishment", and the agent is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "we".
(فَأَغْوَيْناكُمْ إِنَّا كُنَّا غاوِينَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; أغويناكم is a verb, agent and direct object; and this is the fifth answer. ان and its noun, and the clause كنا is the khabar; كان and its noun, and غاوين its khabar. (فَإِنَّهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ فِي الْعَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. if you wish to know the fates of the followers and of the leaders who were followed. ان and its noun; يومئذ is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; إذ is an adverb annexed to its like, the tanwīn being a substitute for a clause, i.e. "the day when they question, blame and dispute with one another"; في العذاب is attached to مشتركون, and مشتركون is the khabar of انهم.
(إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِالْمُجْرِمِينَ): إن and its noun; كذلك is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun put before its verb; the clause نفعل is the khabar of إنا; and بالمجرمين is attached to نفعل.

dervis-irab:83-113.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شِيعَتِهِ): In al-Mukhtār: "al-shīʿa are the followers of a man and his supporters." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-shīʿa: the followers and supporters, and every people who gathered upon a matter are a shīʿa. Then al-shīʿa became a name for a particular group; the plural is shiyaʿ, like sidra and sidar, and al-ashyāʿ is the plural of the plural." In al-Asās: "shayyaʿtuhu on the day of his departure (I saw him off); shāyaʿtuka ʿalā kadhā: I followed you in it; they followed one another in the matter, and they are his shīʿa, his shiyaʿ and his ashyāʿ. This boy is shiyaʿ of his brother: born after him. I will come to you tomorrow or shiyaʿahu (the day after). He said:
قال الخليط: غدا تصدّعنا ... أو شيعه أفلا تشيّعنا
(The companion said: tomorrow we part, or the day after it; will you not see us off?)
I stayed with him a month or shiyaʿ of a month (about a month); he had a hundred men with him or shiyaʿ of that (about that); they alighted at such-and-such a place or shiyaʿahu (near it). The report and the secret spread (shāʿa) and its owner spread it (ashāʿahu); a man mishyāʿ midhyāʿ (a blabber); a drop of milk dripped into water and spread (tashayyaʿa) in it: it dispersed. The she-camel scattered (ashāʿat) her urine; the horses came shawāʾiʿ: scattered; the camels dispersed (tashāyaʿat); he has a share in the house shāʾiʿ and mushāʿ (undivided). Shayyaʿa bi-l-ibil and shāyaʿa bihā: he called to the camels, and from it the shepherd's blower is called al-shiyāʿ; the guide called to them (shāyaʿa bihim) and they saw the guidance: he called out to them. Of the figurative: we followed up (shayyaʿnā) the month of Ramadan with the fast of the six days; and the fire was kindled (shuyyiʿat) with firewood; and 'give me shiyāʿan', as you say shabāban, for what is kindled with and set ablaze; and shayyaʿa this with this: he strengthened it with it. Al-Rāʿī said:
إليك يقطع أجواز الفلاة بنا ... نصّ تشيعه الصّهب المراسيل
(Towards you a swift she-camel at full stretch crosses the mid-stretches of the wilderness with us, followed by the reddish, fast-pacing camels.)
A man mushayyaʿ al-qalb is a brave one, whose heart has been fortified by what lets him ride every terror. Grey hair spread (shāʿa) over his head. And may Allah the Exalted accompany you (shāʿakum) with peace, and may peace accompany you. He said:
ألا يا نخلة في ذات عرق ... برود الظل شاعكم السلام
(O palm tree at Dhāt ʿIrq, of cool shade, may peace accompany you.)"
A glimpse of the Shīʿa:
The statement of the author of al-Miṣbāḥ, "a name for a particular group", means the Shīʿa, the oldest of the Islamic sects. They appeared with their political doctrine at the end of the age of ʿUthmān, and it grew and flourished in the time of ʿAlī. The basis of this doctrine is that the imamate is not among the public interests that are entrusted to the consideration of the community, whose holder is determined by its appointment; rather, it is a pillar of the religion and a foundation of Islam, and it is not permissible for a prophet to neglect it and entrust it to the community; rather he must appoint the imam for them, and he must be immune from major and minor sins, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was the caliph chosen by the Prophet and the best of the Companions. It has many sects, for which one should consult al-Milal wa-l-Niḥal of al-Shahrastānī and al-Faṣl fī l-Milal wa-l-Niḥal of Ibn Ḥazm.
(فَراغَ): he inclined in secret. Its origin is from rawaghān of the fox, which is its going back and forth and its lack of steadiness. In al-Mukhtār: "rāgha al-thaʿlab (of the pattern qāla) and rawaghānan with two fatḥas; the noun from it is al-rawāgh with fatḥa; and arāgha and irtāgha, i.e. he sought and wanted; and rāgha ilā kadhā: he inclined to it secretly and swerved. His saying, the Exalted: 'So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand', i.e. he approached; and al-Farrāʾ said: he inclined towards them. And so-and-so dodges (yurāwigh) in the matter, murāwagha."
(يَزِفُّونَ): they hurry in walking, from the zafīf of the ostrich. Yazifūna is from azaffa when he enters into zafīf, or from azaffahu when he made him carry on at zafīf, i.e. some of them urge on others. In al-Asās: "The bride was conducted (zuffat) to her husband, and this is the night of the zifāf; the male ostrich ran (zaffa) and zafzafa; the wind blew (zaffat) and zafzafat, zafīfan and zafzafatan, which is the speed of blowing and flying with a sound; a wind zafzaf; the wind moved him (zafzafathu) and he spent the night buffeted. Salāma ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Yanbuʿī recited to me in Mecca on the day of the departure:
فبتّ مزفزفا قد أنشبتني ... رسيسة ورد بينهم أحاحا
لعلمي أن صرف البين يضحي ... ينيل العين قرّتها لماحا
(So I spent the night buffeted; a lingering touch of fever among them had clung to me, burning. For I knew that the turning of separation would end by granting the eye its coolness in glimpses.)
And of the figurative: zaffū ilayhi: they hurried to him; and of the flighty-minded it is said: 'his ostrich-chick has run' (qad zaffa raʾluhu); and I came to him zaffatan or zaffatayn, once or twice, which is the single instance of zafīf, just as the single instance of murūr (passing) is marra."
(وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ): he threw him down on his side, so that one of his sides fell on the ground, out of humility before undertaking the matter with patience and endurance. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-jabīn is the side of the forehead, from the bald-temple part to the temple; they are two jabīns, on the right of the forehead and its left; this was said by al-Azharī, Ibn Fāris and others. So the forehead is between two jabīns; its plural is jubun with two dammas, like barīd and burud, and ajbina like asliḥa." And in al-Qāmūs: "tallahu tallan (of the pattern qatala), so he is matlūl and talīl: he threw him down, or cast him on his neck and cheek."
(الْجَحِيمِ): the fire of intense fuel; it is also said that every fire upon fire and ember upon ember is jaḥīm. In al-Qāmūs: "al-jaḥīm: the fire of intense blazing, and every fire some of which is on top of some, like al-jaḥma (also with damma); and every great fire in a pit; and the place of intense heat, like al-jāḥim; jaḥamahā, like manaʿahā: he kindled it, so it blazed (jaḥamat, like karumat) jaḥūman, and like fariḥa, jaḥman and jaḥīman: it was agitated; and al-jāḥim is the intensely burning ember."

* I'rab:
(وَإِنَّ مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ لَإِبْراهِيمَ) The wāw is a conjunction, conjoining the second story to the first; you may also make it resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), so that the clause is resumptive, introduced to begin the story of Abraham after the story of Noah. inna is a particle resembling the verb; من شيعته is its fronted khabar; the shifted lām; and إبراهيم is its delayed noun.
(إِذْ جاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ) You may attach the adverb to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; or you may attach it to the meaning of derivation in "shīʿa", so that it is governed by it for the meaning of following it contains. The clause جاء is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to Abraham; ربه is the direct object; بقلب is attached to جاء; and سليم is an adjective.
(إِذْ قالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ ماذا تَعْبُدُونَ) The second adverb is a badal (substitute) for the first adverb. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be an adverb of سليم or of جاء. The clause قال is in the position of genitive by annexation; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; لأبيه is attached to قال; and the parsing of ماذا has been given many times: ما is a mubtadaʾ and ذا a relative noun as khabar; or the whole is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a fronted object of تعبدون. The clause تعبدون has no position on the first view, and the clause ماذا is the content of the saying on the second.
(أَإِفْكاً آلِهَةً دُونَ اللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ) The hamza is for rebuking denial (istifhām inkārī). For the accusative of إفكا there are several aspects. One is that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "do you want gods besides Allah out of falsehood?" so آلهة is the direct object and دون الله an adverb attached to تريدون; the dependents of the verb were fronted out of concern for it, because he is confronting them with the fact that they are in falsehood and error. Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Jalāl began with this aspect. The second is that it is a direct object of تريدون, and آلهة is a badal from it, making them the very falsehood by exaggeration, so he substituted them for it and explained it by them. The third is that it is a ḥāl from the agent of تريدون, i.e. "do you want gods while lying, or being people of falsehood?"
(فَما ظَنُّكُمْ بِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun for denial and rebuke, i.e. you have no cause or excuse that carries you to such an opinion; it is in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ; ظنكم is its khabar; and برب العالمين is attached to ظنكم. In al-Bayḍāwī: "The meaning is a denial of whatever could necessitate an opinion, let alone a certainty, that would bar one from worshipping Him, or permit associating partners with Him, or imply security from His punishment, by way of constraint, and it is like the proof for what precedes it."
(فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةً فِي النُّجُومِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; نظر is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; نظرة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and في النجوم is attached to نظر. It was said that the speech has an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in the science of the stars". He did not say "إلى النجوم" although naẓara is transitive with ilā, because "fī" comes in the sense of "ilā", as in His saying, the Exalted, «فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم», i.e. to them; and it was said that naẓara is made to include the meaning of "he thought", which is transitive with fī.
(فَقالَ إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قال is a past verb with a latent agent; إني: inna and its noun; and سقيم is its khabar; inna and what is within its scope are in the position of accusative, the content of the saying. The discussion on permitting lying to Abraham will come.
(فَتَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ مُدْبِرِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; تولوا is a past verb and agent; عنه is attached to تولوا; and مدبرين is a ḥāl from the wāw in تولوا.
(فَراغَ إِلى آلِهَتِهِمْ فَقالَ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; راغ is a past verb and agent; إلى آلهتهم is attached to راغ; فقال is conjoined to راغ; the hamza is for interrogation and لا is negative; تأكلون is an imperfect verb in the nominative and an agent; and the interrogative clause is the content of the saying.
(ما لَكُمْ لا تَنْطِقُونَ) ما is an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ and لكم its khabar; the clause لا تنطقون is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and the clause مالكم is the content of an omitted saying, the implied form being "and they did not speak, so he said: what is the matter with you that you do not speak?"
(فَراغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْباً بِالْيَمِينِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element, its implied form being "so they did not answer, and he turned"; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to راغ; ضربا is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "he turned upon them striking", or a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "he struck a striking", and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and باليمين is attached to ضربا or to its governor.
(فَأَقْبَلُوا إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أقبلوا is a past verb and the wāw its agent; إليه is attached to أقبلوا; and the clause يزفون is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of أقبلوا; it is permissible that إليه be attached to it.
(قالَ أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ) قال is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he"; the hamza is for rebuking denial; تعبدون is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is the agent; ما is the direct object; and the clause تنحتون is a ṣila (relative clause) whose returning pronoun is omitted. It is permissible that ما be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "your carving"; it is permissible that it be an indefinite qualified noun, i.e. "what you carve"; and it was said to be interrogative for rebuke, i.e. "and what thing do you do?"
(وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَما تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause خلقكم is the khabar and the kāf the direct object; the wāw is a conjunction; ما may be relative or a maṣdar particle; and it was said to be interrogative for rebuke, i.e. "and what thing do you do?"; and it was said to be negative, i.e. the work in reality is not yours, so you do nothing. More discussion of this construction, over which the people of the Sunna and the Muʿtazila disagreed, will come. The clause والله خلقكم is a ḥāl, and its meaning is: do you worship the idols in a state contrary to that, namely that Allah is the Creator of you and of them all? The wāw may also be resumptive, with the clause resumptive.
(قالُوا ابْنُوا لَهُ بُنْياناً فَأَلْقُوهُ فِي الْجَحِيمِ) قالوا is a verb and agent; ابنوا is an imperative and the wāw its agent, and the clause is the content of the saying; له is attached to ابنوا; بنيانا is the direct object; فألقوه is conjoined to ابنوا, an imperative with the wāw as agent and the hāʾ as direct object; and في الجحيم is attached to ألقوه.
(فَأَرادُوا بِهِ كَيْداً فَجَعَلْناهُمُ الْأَسْفَلِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أرادوا is a past verb and agent; به is attached to أرادوا; كيدا is the direct object; فجعلناهم is conjoined to فأرادوا, a verb, agent and first direct object; and الأسفلين is the second direct object of جعلناهم.
(وَقالَ إِنِّي ذاهِبٌ إِلى رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ) The wāw is a conjunction upon an omitted element, its implied form being "so he came out of the fire safe, and said"; inna and its noun; ذاهب is its khabar; إلى ربي is attached to ذاهب; the sīn is a particle of futurity; and يهدين is an imperfect verb in the nominative by an implied damma on the yāʾ, the nūn being the protective nūn, and the pronoun yāʾ, omitted in observance of the verse-endings, is the direct object, i.e. "sa-yahdīnī". The meaning of his going to his Lord will come in the section on benefits.
(رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) رب is the one addressed, annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker, and similar cases have preceded it; هب is a verb of supplication and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "You"; لي is attached to هب; and من الصالحين is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "a child from among the righteous".
(فَبَشَّرْناهُ بِغُلامٍ حَلِيمٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element, its implied form being "so We answered him"; بشرناه is a past verb, agent and direct object; بغلام is attached to بشرناه; and حليم is an adjective. In the speech is a concision (ījāz) that will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; لما is temporal (ḥīniyya) or connective (rābiṭa); بلغ is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he"; and the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "If you say: to what is معه attached? I say: it cannot be other than attached to بلغ, or to السعي, or to an omitted element. It is not valid to attach it to بلغ, since that would require that the two of them reached the limit of striving together; nor to السعي, because the complement of a maṣdar does not precede it. So what remains is that it is an explanation: as though, when He said 'when he reached the striving', i.e. the limit at which he is able to strive, it was said 'with whom?', and He said 'with his father'. The meaning of specifying the father is that he is the gentlest of people towards him and the most compassionate to him, whereas another might have been harsh in making him work, and he could not bear it, because his strength was not yet firm and his frame not yet hardened."
(قالَ يا بُنَيَّ إِنِّي أَرى فِي الْمَنامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى) The clause قال has no position because it is the response to لما; يا is a vocative particle; بني is the one addressed, annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker; inna and its noun, with the clause أرى as its khabar; في المنام is attached to أرى; أن and its noun, with the clause أذبحك as khabar; أن and what follows it stand in the place of the two objects of the dream-sense raʾā. فانظر: the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; انظر is an imperative whose agent is obligatorily latent, its implied form being "you"; and in ماذا ترى it is permissible that ماذا be a compound interrogative, so that it is accusative by ترى, and what follows it is in the position of accusative by انظر because it is suspended (muʿallaqa) for it; it is also permissible that ما be interrogative and ذا relative, so ماذا is mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is also suspended; and that ماذا be in the sense of "that which", so that it is governed by انظر. ترى is an imperfect verb from raʾy (opinion), not from seeing with the eye, nor the one transitive to two objects, but like your saying "he holds the opinion (yarā raʾy) of the Khawārij".
(قالَ يا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ ما تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ) يا is a vocative particle; أبت is the one addressed, annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker, for which the tāʾ is a substitute, and this has been fully discussed repeatedly; the tāʾ is in the position of genitive because that for which it substitutes is so. افعل is an imperative whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; ما is a relative noun, the object of افعل; the clause تؤمر is the ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "what you are commanded with", so the preposition was omitted as in your saying "amartuka al-khayra" (I commanded you the good), "so do what you were commanded with". It is permissible that ما be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "your command", with the maṣdar annexed to its object. The sīn is a particle of futurity; تجدني is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the nūn the protective nūn, the agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and the yāʾ the direct object; and من الصابرين is in the place of the second object.
(فَلَمَّا أَسْلَما وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal or connective; أسلما is a past verb and the alif the agent, i.e. they submitted, yielded and complied with the command of Allah. وتله: the wāw is a conjunction; تله is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he", i.e. Abraham, and the hāʾ is the direct object; and للجبين is attached to an omitted ḥāl. The response to لما is omitted, its implied form being "their patience became manifest", or "We multiplied their reward", or "what happened happened, of what the situation itself declares". The Kufans and al-Akhfash said that the response is وتله للجبين, with the wāw redundant; and it was said "وناديناه", with the wāw also redundant; but the first is preferable.
(وَنادَيْناهُ أَنْ يا إِبْراهِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; ناديناه is a verb, agent and direct object; أن is explicative (mufassira), because the calling contains the meaning of saying without its letters; يا is a vocative particle; and إبراهيم is a single proper-name one addressed, indeclinable on the damma.
(قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) قد is a particle of affirmation; صدقت is a verb and agent; الرؤيا is the direct object; inna and its noun; كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar fronted before its governor; and the clause نجزي المحسنين is the khabar of inna. The clause inna gives the reason for the relief bestowed on them after hardship and the hope after despair.
(إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ الْبَلاءُ الْمُبِينُ) inna and its noun; the shifted lām; هو is a mubtadaʾ or a separation pronoun; البلاء is the khabar of هو or the khabar of inna; and المبين is an adjective of البلاء.
(وَفَدَيْناهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; فديناه is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is conjoined to ناديناه; بذبح is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فديناه; al-dhibḥ is the name of what is slaughtered, whether a ram or a mountain goat; and عظيم is an adjective of ذبح.
(وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ) The parsing of the like of this verse has preceded. The object of تركنا is omitted, and في الآخرين is an adjective of this omitted element, i.e. "good praise".
(سَلامٌ عَلى إِبْراهِيمَ) سلام is a mubtadaʾ and على إبراهيم the khabar; beginning with an indefinite is permitted because of the meaning of supplication in it; and the clause سلام على إبراهيم is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "this is said to him among the later generations".
(كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; نجزي المحسنين is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object.
(إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) inna and its noun; من عبادنا is the khabar; المؤمنين is an adjective; and the clause is explanatory of cause, with no position.
(وَبَشَّرْناهُ بِإِسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; بشرناه is a verb, agent and direct object; بإسحاق is attached to بشرناه; نبيا is a ḥāl from Isaac; and من الصالحين is an adjective of نبيا or a second ḥāl. It comes by way of praise and commendation, because every prophet must be righteous.
(وَبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلى إِسْحاقَ) وباركنا is conjoined to what preceded; عليه is attached to باركنا; and على إسحاق is conjoined to عليه.
(وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ وَظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ مُبِينٌ) من ذريتهما is a fronted khabar; محسن is a delayed mubtadaʾ; ظالم is conjoined to محسن; لنفسه is attached to ظالم; and مبين is an adjective of ظالم.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains various arts, of which we cite the most important in what follows:
1- In His saying "Then he said: I am sick" is the art of allusion and hint (ramz and īmāʾ). It is when the speaker wishes to conceal a matter in his speech, so he hints at it within it, either to obscure it for the one addressed and clear himself and disclaim responsibility, or so that by means of it one may be guided to the way of drawing out what he concealed in his speech. The people of Abraham were astrologers, so he led them to think that he inferred from a sign in the science of astrology that he would fall sick, and said "I am sick", i.e. about to be sick, namely with the plague, which was the most common of illnesses among them, and they feared contagion. He said that so that they would feel fear and disperse from him; so they fled from him to their festival and left him in the house of the idols with no one with him, and he did to the idols what he did. The outward sense of the speech may suggest that he thereby committed the offence of lying, whereas prophets are immune from it. The correct view is that lying is forbidden except when one speaks obliquely and equivocates; and Abraham intended that whoever has death at his neck is sick. From it is the proverb "Safety is disease enough" (kafā bi-l-salāma dāʾan). And Labīd said:
كانت قناتي لا تلين لغامز ... فألانها الإصباح والإمساء
فدعوت ربي بالسلامة جاهدا ... ليصحني فإذا السلامة داء
(My spear-shaft would not bend for one who pressed it, then morning and evening made it supple. So I prayed to my Lord earnestly for safety, that He keep me sound, and behold, safety is itself a disease.)
[Translator's note: the source prints «فألا منها» in the first verse; the verse is known as «فألانها».] Labīd describes his strength in the time of youth, then his weakness in old age with the succession of the times upon him, and that he asked for a long term of life, which became the cause of his decay. Al-qanāt is the spear; he borrowed it for his uprightness or strength by way of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), and suppleness (al-līna) and pressing (al-ghamz) are an embellishment (tarshīḥ) of the metaphor; al-ghamz is feeling with the hand. A man died and the people gathered around him saying "he died while healthy", and a Bedouin said: "Is he healthy who has death at his neck?" It was also said that he meant by his saying "I am sick" a sickness of the soul because of your unbelief; although some people have permitted it in deception in war, in taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation), in pleasing a spouse, and in reconciling disputants and those who have cut off relations. More on this unique story will come in the section on benefits.
2- Concision (al-ījāz):
In His saying "So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy" is a concision by brevity (ījāz qiṣar), whose definition has preceded. This concise glad tiding contains three things: that the child is male, that he would reach the age of forbearance, and that he would be forbearing. And what forbearance is a clearer proof of that than his forbearance when his father presented slaughter to him: he was not agitated, did not falter and did not object to his father's will, but said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient", and then submitted to that, and it never occurred to his mind that Allah would ransom him and would prepare the ram of ransom for him.

* Benefits:
1- Who is the one sacrificed?
The exegetes differed about the one commanded to be slaughtered. From Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar and a group of the Followers: it was Ishmael, and their proof for it is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am the son of the two sacrificed ones", and a Bedouin said to him "O son of the two sacrificed ones", and he smiled. He was asked about that and said: when ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib dug the well of Zamzam he vowed to Allah that if Allah made its matter easy for him he would sacrifice one of his sons. The lot fell on ʿAbdallāh, and his maternal uncles prevented him and said to him: we will ransom him for a hundred camels. So he ransomed him with a hundred camels; and the second is Ishmael. They also argued that Allah described him with patience, not Isaac, in His saying, the Exalted: «وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين», which is his patience with the slaughter. From ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn Masʿūd, al-ʿAbbās, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima and others: it was Isaac, and this is the view of the People of the two Books, the Jews and Christians. The argument for it is that Allah the Exalted informed His intimate friend Abraham, when he migrated to Syria, that he asked Him for a child, then followed that with the glad tiding of a forbearing boy, then mentioned his dream of slaughtering that boy who had been given as glad tiding. The letter of Jacob to Joseph also indicates it, in which it is said: "From Jacob Israel of Allah, son of Isaac the sacrificed of Allah, son of Abraham the intimate friend of Allah." Al-Zajjāj said: "Allah knows best which of them was the sacrificed one." This is a third position, which is to hold back from deciding between the two views and to entrust the knowledge of it to Allah the Exalted. Perhaps this is better, since this question is not among the doctrines we are charged with knowing; it is among what is beneficial to know and not harmful to be ignorant of, and Allah knows best. The exegetes and historians have long discussion of the story of the sacrifice, to be consulted in the longer works.
2- A debate between the people of the Sunna and the Muʿtazila:
There is a debate between the people of the Sunna and the Muʿtazila which it behoves us to summarise for its charm and its close connection with i'rab. Al-Zamakhsharī asked about His saying, the Exalted: «والله خلقكم وما تعملون»: "How can one and the same thing be created by Allah the Exalted and also made by them?" and he answered that this is as one says "the carpenter made the door", where the intended is making its shape, not its substance. Likewise the idols: their substances are created by Allah the Exalted, while their shapes and forms are made by them. "If you say: what prevents you from making ما a maṣdar particle, not a relative, so that the meaning is 'Allah created you and your work', as the Jabriyya say?" He answered: "The nearest thing by which this question is refuted, after its refutation by rational proofs, is that the meaning of the verse refuses it, for Allah the Exalted argued against them that He created the worshipper and the worshipped, so how can the created worship the created, given that the worshipper in both is the one who made the form of the worshipped?" He said: "Had you said 'Allah created you and your work', the speech would have no correspondence (ṭibāq); and another thing: that His saying «وما تعملون» is explained in His saying «أتعبدون ما تنحتون», and it is not said that this ما is relative, so distinguishing between them is arbitrary and partisan." He said: "If you say: make it relative, meaning 'what you do of your deeds', then it agrees with the first in being relative, so I am not obliged to distinguish between them?" He answered: "Rather both obligations are around your neck, and only submission to the truth will release them: even if you make it relative, it applies in your view to the maṣdar which is the substance of the joining, and in that is a disjointing of the composition and a cutting off, as if you had made it a maṣdar particle."
Ibn al-Munayyir followed him up and said: "It is necessary to take it as a maṣdar. That is because they did not worship these idols as stones unshaped; had it been so, they would not have cooperated in shaping them, nor singled out a stone for their worship over another stone. So it indicates that they worship them only with respect to their shapes and forms, which are the effect of their work; in reality they worshipped their own work, and the argument is sound against them, that they are like it, even though the worshipped is the acquisition of the worshipper and his work. So it is clear that the argument stands against them, on the assumption that ما is a maṣdar, in the clearest and most eloquent way. When that is established, let his speech be pursued in refutation. As for his saying that it is relative and that what is meant by their making of them is making their shapes, it contradicts the outward sense, for it needs an omitted muḍāf in a place of despair, its implied form being 'Allah created you and what you make of its shape and form', unlike the aspect given by the people of the Sunna, which needs no omission whatever. Then, if the worshipped is made the substance itself, how does it fit their rebuke by showing that the worshipped is the work of the worshipper, while agreeing that the substances of the idols are not their work? What is their work, the shape, is not their worshipped object on this interpretation, and what is their worshipped object, the substance of the idol, is not their work; so it has no stable footing that the worshipped, on his interpretation, is the work of the worshipper, whereas on what we have set out it is plain. As for his saying that the correspondence breaks down on the interpretation of the people of the Sunna between «ما تنحتون» and «ما تعملون», it is not correct; for we may take the first as a maṣdar, and that in reality they worshipped only their carving, because these idols, being stones before carving, they did not worship; when they worked carving into them they worshipped them; so in reality they worshipped nothing but their carving, which is their work. The correspondence is then achieved, and the constraint on this view is more eloquent and firmer. Had it been as he says, the argument would have stood for them, and they would have said, as al-Zamakhsharī says, confronting His saying «Allah created you and what you do»: 'No, and no honour! Allah does not create what we do, for we knew the shaping and the forming, and this Allah did not create', and they would have found a pretext for rushing into the argument."
[Translator's note: the source text of this passage is evidently corrupt in places (for example «جوهر الضم» and «في موضع اليأس»); it is translated as written.]
3- The meaning of going to his Lord:
There is disagreement on the meaning of His saying «إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين». Most hold that this verse is a basis for emigration (hijra) and seclusion, i.e. "I am emigrating from the land of my people and my birthplace to where I can worship my Lord, for He will guide me to the right path." And in the sīn of futurity is an announcement that the act will certainly occur.

dervis-irab:35-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِكَأْسٍ): A glass vessel with wine in it is called a كأس, and the wine itself is also called a كأس. Al-Aʿshā said:
وكأس شربت على لذة ... وأخرى تداويت منها بها
لكي يعلم الناس أني امرؤ ... أتيت المعيشة من بابها
(Many a cup I drank for pleasure, and another I took as a remedy for the first by means of it, so that people might know I am a man who has come to livelihood by its door.)
الكأس is applied to the glass vessel containing wine and, figuratively, to the wine, which is well known. It is feminine, as shown by its pronoun and adjective, and its plural is كئوس, أكؤس, كاسات and كئاس. Al-Aʿshā is saying: "Many a cup I drank with pleasure or for the sake of pleasure and it harmed me, so I drank another cup, curing myself of the first by it, so that people would know that I am experienced in affairs." He alluded to that by his saying «أتيت المعيشة من بابها», likening livelihood together with its suitable means to a house with a door, by way of the implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya), the affirming of the door being a takhyīl (imaginative figure). Abū Nuwās took from this meaning his famous verse:
دع عنك لومي فإن اللوم إغراء ... وداوني بالتي كانت هي الداء
(Leave your blame, for blame is an incitement, and cure me with that which was the disease.)
It is related from al-Akhfash: "Every كأس in the Qur'an is wine." Abū Ḥayyān said: "الكأس is whatever is of glass with wine or the like of the nabīdh drinks in it, and it is not called a كأس unless there is wine in it; otherwise it is a قدح (goblet). Wine is sometimes called كأس, by naming a thing with the name of its container."
(مَعِينٍ): Abū Ḥayyān said: "An active participle from معن with ḍamma on the ʿayn, like شريف from شرف", i.e. from a flowing drink, or a flowing river, visible to the eyes or issuing from springs; it is an adjective of water, from عان الماء when the water gushed forth. The wine of Paradise is described with it because it flows like water. We shall expand on this word because it is much used today for a geometrical figure. We say: it is stated in the lexicons in the root م-ع-ن as follows: معن يمعن, from the pattern of فتح, said of water; and معن يمعن from the pattern of ظرف, maʿnan and maʿūnan: it flowed with an easy flow, so it is "maʿīn". معن الفرس: the horse stretched out in its running. معن المطر الأرض: the rain followed continuously upon the land and watered it. معن يمعن, from the pattern of شرب, maʿnan, said of a place or plant: it was watered. المعين is flowing water, and "ماء معين" means flowing water. Under the root ع-ي-ن: "الماء المعين is the visible water that the eye sees flowing on the face of the earth; and عين معيونة is a spring that has abundant supply of water." As for the geometric figure, it is most likely "al-muʿayyin", with ḍamma on the mīm and a shadda on the kasra-bearing yāʾ, an active participle from عين with doubled yāʾ; in geometry it is a flat figure with four equal straight sides surrounding it, not right-angled (a rhombus).
(غَوْلٌ): that which destroys the mind. One says غاله يغوله غولا when he spoiled it; from it is the ghoul (الغول) of the Arabs' tall tales, and in their proverbs "الغضب غول الحلم" (anger is the ghoul of forbearance). غالته الخمر: he drank it and it carried off his reason or the soundness of his body. الغول is a verbal noun, and also headache, drunkenness, the distance of a desert, hardship, a dip in the ground, and much soil.
(يُنْزَفُونَ): in the passive, from نزف الشارب when his reason is gone; a drunk is called نزيف and منزوف; and it is said of one stabbed نزف فمات when all his blood came out; and نزحت الركية حتى نزفتها (I drained the well until I exhausted it). Among their proverbs: "أجبن من المنزوف ضرطا" (more cowardly than one who is drained by breaking wind).
The story of this proverb: two men went out into a desert and a tree appeared to them. One said: "I see people who have set an ambush for us." The other said: "They are only ten (ʿashara)", but he thought he said "ten", and he began to say "What use are two against ten?" and kept breaking wind until he died. It is related in another version that some women who had no man married one of them to a man who used to sleep through the morning; when they came to him with a morning draught and woke him, he said: "If you had waked me, I would have attacked it." When they saw that, they said: "Our companion is surely brave; come, let us test him." They came to him and woke him, and he said as was his habit, and they said: "These are the forelocks of the horses." He began to say "The horses! The horses!" and kept breaking wind until he died. There are other sayings on it that we have passed over.
In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "نزفت ماء البئر when you drained it entirely, and نزفت it (the well) is both transitive and intransitive, and نزفت also in the passive."
(قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ): those who restrict their gaze to their husbands and do not look at others; it may be of the pattern of the resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), i.e. "restricting their glances", like "fluent of tongue", and it may be of the active participle in its basic sense; the difference between the two will come in the I'rab.
(عِينٌ): wide-eyed; the plural of عيناء; and "wide-eyed" (النجل) is the plural of نجلاء, she whose eye-slit is wide with a width that is not excessive.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا إِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ): إن and its noun, and the clause كانوا is its khabar; كان and its noun; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause قيل is in the position of genitive by annexation; لهم is attached to قيل; the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "it"; the clause لا إله إلا الله is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "Say: there is no god but Allah" — the parsing of the word of tawḥīd has preceded in detail; the clause يستكبرون is the khabar of كانوا; and the apodosis of إذا is omitted, indicated by what precedes.
(وَيَقُولُونَ أَإِنَّا لَتارِكُوا آلِهَتِنا لِشاعِرٍ مَجْنُونٍ): ويقولون is conjoined to يستكبرون; the hamza is for denying interrogation; ان and its noun, the shifted lām, and تاركو is the khabar of إن; لشاعر is attached to تاركوا, i.e. for the sake of a poet; and مجنون is an adjective.
(بَلْ جاءَ بِالْحَقِّ وَصَدَّقَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ): A rejecting rejection; جاء is a verb with a latent agent; بالحق is attached to جاء; and صدق المرسلين is conjoined to جاء بالحق.
(إِنَّكُمْ لَذائِقُوا الْعَذابِ الْأَلِيمِ): إن and its noun — the secret of this iltifāt will come in the chapter on Rhetoric — the shifted lām, and ذائقو العذاب is the khabar of ان and الأليم an adjective.
(وَما تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; تجزون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw the nāʾib fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is a second direct object, and it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of what"; the clause كنتم تعملون is the ṣila of ما, and the clause تعملون the khabar of كنتم.
(إِلَّا عِبادَ اللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ): إلا is a particle of exception with the meaning of "but" (lākin), because the exception is discontinuous; عباد الله is excepted from the wāw in تجزون; and المخلصين is an adjective of عباد الله. (أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ رِزْقٌ مَعْلُومٌ): A resumptive utterance to establish what has been prepared for the sincere servants of Allah. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; لهم a predicate put forward; رزق a mubtadaʾ put later; معلوم an adjective of رزق; and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "its time", or "known" by the characteristics by which it is distinguished, among them permanence, pure pleasure, goodness of taste, and beauty of الرداء and appearance «[Translator's note: the source reads "وحسن الرداء والمنظر"; the word الرداء (literally "cloak") is left as written, its sense here being uncertain]». The clause لهم رزق معلوم is the khabar of أولئك. (فَواكِهُ وَهُمْ مُكْرَمُونَ): فواكه is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān of الرزق, a badal of the whole for the whole; more of the merits of this badal will come in the chapter on Rhetoric. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and مكرمون its khabar. (فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ): attached to مكرمون, or it is a second khabar, or both are attached to an omitted element in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ): على سرر is attached to متقابلين, and متقابلين is a ḥāl, or both are a ḥāl; and the speech contains a depiction of drinking gatherings, more of which will come in the chapter on Rhetoric.
(يُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِكَأْسٍ مِنْ مَعِينٍ): The clause is an adjective of مكرمون, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in متقابلين, or a resumptive clause; عليهم is attached to يطاف; بكأس stands in the place of the mafʿūl muṭlaq — the discussion of this has preceded in detail — and من معين is an adjective of كأس. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: every كأس in the Qur'an is wine.
(بَيْضاءَ لَذَّةٍ لِلشَّارِبِينَ): بيضاء is a second adjective of كأس and لذة a third adjective of كأس, described by a verbal noun for intensification, or on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessing pleasure", or it is the feminine of اللذ; one says لذ الشيء, so it is لذ and لذيذ, like your saying رجل طب, i.e. طبيب. He said:
لذّ كطعم الصرخدي تركته ... بأرض العدا من خشية الحدثان
(A delight like the taste of Ṣarkhadī wine I left in the land of the enemies, for fear of misfortunes.)
اللذ is an adjective, and اللذة is feminine, being a noun for the state subsisting in the soul and a noun for the delightful thing. الصرخد is a place in al-Shām to which the drink is ascribed; الحدثان is a verbal noun like الحدث except that it indicates renewal and repetition. He says: many a delightful thing — meaning sleep — whose taste is like the taste of the drink I left in the land of the enemies for fear that disliked things would befall me. (لا فِيها غَوْلٌ وَلا هُمْ عَنْها يُنْزَفُونَ): The clause is a fourth adjective of كأس; لا is negative; فيها a predicate put forward; غول a mubtadaʾ put later; ولا is a conjunction; هم a mubtadaʾ; عنها attached to ينزفون; and the clause ينزفون is the khabar of هم and is passive. (وَعِنْدَهُمْ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ عِينٌ): The wāw is a conjunction; the adverb is attached to an omitted predicate put forward; قاصرات الطرف is a mubtadaʾ put later; الطرف is a muḍāf ilayhi, nominative in position if قاصرات is a resembling adjective, or accusative in position if قاصرات is an active participle; and عين is an adjective of قاصرات الطرف. (كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ): A second adjective of قاصرات, or, if قاصرات is considered an adjective, a third adjective; كأن and its noun; بيض its khabar; مكنون an adjective; the discussion of this simile will come in the chapter on Rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift):
In His saying «إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم» there is a shift from the third person to the second, to confront them with wrath, and that it has reached the utmost of its limits and bounds.
2- Concision (ījāz):
In His saying «فواكه» and its being a badal of رزق there is ījāz qaṣr (concision by condensation), which indicated that they have reached the utmost that a wisher can wish for and that a delighted one can delight in. The fruits are equal to the provision, resembling bread and meat, because their eating is not to maintain and preserve health but for enjoyment and fruit-taking, for their bodies there are firm, not assailed by frailty nor reached by weakness or languor.
There is another concision in His saying «معلوم», for this word stands in for the times and durations, and includes the evenings, the late afternoons and the early mornings, as it stands in for the differing tastes and the diverse scents that differ in appearance and agree in goodness and in the intoxicating spreading of their fragrance.
3- Embodiment (tajsīd):
The wonderful artistic image appears in His saying «على سرر متقابلين»; there is nothing more delightful to drinkers in the hours of the morning or evening draught, in early morning and evenings, than that they face one another, for facing is more complete for joy and more conducive to bliss; and their exchange of conversations and enjoyments will also come.
4- Concision also:
In the description of the wine there is an eloquent concision, namely His saying «لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون», for these two words combined all the defects of the wine of the people of this world on account of which it was forbidden: colic, headache, hangover, rowdiness, idle talk, sinfulness, and the like.
5- Unbound simile (tashbīh mursal):
In His saying «كأنهن بيض مكنون» there is an unbound simile. What is meant by "eggs" here is ostrich eggs, and "مكنون" is from كننته, i.e. I put it in a shelter (kinn). The Arabs liken a woman to it in colour, which is a whiteness tinged with some yellow, which we today call the camphor colour. The first to liken a woman to an egg was Imruʾ al-Qays in his verse:
وبيضة خدر لا يرام خباؤها ... تمتعت من لهو بها غير معجل
(Many a maiden of the chamber, whose tent cannot be approached, I enjoyed in play with her, unhurried.)
Women are likened to eggs in three respects. The first is health and freedom from menstruation, and from it is the verse of al-Farazdaq:
خرجن إلي لم يطمثن قبلي ... وهن أصح من بيض النعام
(They came out to me, none touched before me, and they are healthier than ostrich eggs.)
The second is protection and covering, because the bird protects its eggs and fortifies them; the third is clarity and purity of colour, because the egg is clear and pure in colour when under the bird. This is one of the similes that the moderns today have turned away from, though it is wonderful in itself, because the environment no longer finds such similes palatable.
Simile between differing environments:
To clarify the difference between environments we say: the Arabs found good the likening of fingers and fingertips to a worm that lives in sand, whose group is called "daughters of the dune" (banāt al-naqā). From that is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays: وتعطو برخص غير شثن كأنه ... أساريع ظبي أو مساويك إسحل
(And she reaches out with a soft hand, not coarse, as if it were the sand-worms of a gazelle-haunt, or the tooth-sticks of the isḥil tree.)
He likened the fingertip to the أسروعة, i.e. the sand worm. Dhū l-Rumma said:
خزاعيب أمثال كأن بنانها ... بنات النقا تخفي مرارا وتظهر
(Graceful ones, whose fingertips are like the daughters of the dune, hiding many times and appearing.)
So it is like the finest fingertips in softness, whiteness, length, evenness, slenderness, and in the redness of the tip as if it were a dyed nail. But the soul soon found this simile distasteful, and Abū Nuwās turned away from it by his saying:
تعاطيكها كف كأن بنانها ... إذا اعترضتها العين صف مداري
(A hand hands it to you whose fingertips, when the eye comes across them, are a row of ivory spindles/combs.)
and Ibn al-Rūmī also by his saying:
سقى الله قصرا بالرصافة شاقني ... بأعلاه قصريّ الدلالي رصافي
أشار بقضبان هي الدر قمعت ... يواقيت حمرا فاستباح عفافي
(May Allah water a palace at al-Ruṣāfa, whose top enchanted me — a palace-dweller coquettish, of al-Ruṣāfa. She gestured with branches that are pearls, capped with red rubies, and so she made my chastity lawful to her.)
or the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʿtazz:
أشرن على خوف بأغصان فضة ... مقومة أثمارهن عقيق
(They gestured in fear with branches of silver, straight, whose fruits are carnelian.)
Thus the simile differs with the difference of environments. More of this important discussion will come, and what we have presented suffices for now.

dervis-irab:50-61.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to يطاف عليهم; the meaning is that they drink and converse over the drink, as is the habit of drinkers. He said:
وما بقيت من اللذات إلا ... أحاديث الكرام على المدام
(Of pleasures nothing remains but the conversations of the noble over wine.)
So some of them turn to others. The verse is by al-Farazdaq; he says: no pleasure of the pleasures remains except the pleasure of the conversations of the noble, or no delightful desire remains except the conversations of the noble over wine; and he used the particle of elevation (ʿalā) because the drink is in front of them and the conversation from their mouths is above it. أقبل بعضهم is a verb and agent; على بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقبل; the clause يتساءلون is circumstantial; and the expression in the past form is for emphasis and to indicate certainty of occurrence, which is the custom of Allah in His reports. (قالَ قائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي كانَ لِي قَرِينٌ): قال قائل is a verb and agent; منهم is an adjective of قائل, i.e. from the people of Paradise; إن and its noun, and the clause كان is the khabar; the clause of إن with its noun and khabar is the content of the saying; لي is the predicate of كان put forward, and قرين its noun put later, i.e. "I had in the present abode a companion." (يقول أَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُصَدِّقِينَ): The clause يقول is an adjective of قرين; the hamza is for denying interrogation; إن and its noun, the shifted lām, and من المصدقين is the khabar of إن; and the clause is the content of the saying.
(أَإِذا مِتْنا وَكُنَّا تُراباً وَعِظاماً أَإِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ): The hamza is for denying interrogation; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause متنا is in the position of genitive by annexation; كنا is an incomplete past verb, نا its noun, ترابا its khabar, and عظاما conjoined to ترابا; the hamza is for interrogation; إن and its noun, the shifted lām, and مدينون is the khabar of إن, i.e. "recompensed and reckoned with". (قالَ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونَ): قال is a past verb and the agent a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he", referring to that speaker from the people of Paradise, i.e. he said to his brothers; هل is a particle of interrogation; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and مطلعون its khabar; and the interrogation has the meaning of a command, i.e. "Come, let us look out from the windows of the gardens so that we may see the state of the people of the Fire." (فَاطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ فِي سَواءِ الْجَحِيمِ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; اطلع is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, "he", referring to that speaker; فرآه is a past verb with latent agent and a direct object, i.e. he saw his companion; في سواء الجحيم is attached to رآه, i.e. in the middle of it. You may attach the preposition and its genitive noun to an omitted ḥāl, which is perhaps preferable, i.e. "plunged in the middle of Hell".
(قالَ تَاللَّهِ إِنْ كِدْتَ لَتُرْدِينِ): قال is a past verb with a latent agent; تالله: the tāʾ is a particle of oath and genitive, and it together with its genitive noun is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; إن is the lightened form of the heavy إن; you may let it operate, in which case its noun is omitted, i.e. "you", and the clause كدت is its khabar; or you may let it not operate, in which case the clause كدت is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. We have already said that when إن is lightened it most often enters upon كاد as it enters upon كان and the like, and the lām is the distinguishing lām between it and the negative. تردين is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, "you"; the nūn is the protective nūn; the yāʾ is the direct object; and the yāʾ was dropped in accordance with the practice of the muṣḥaf.
(وَلَوْلا نِعْمَةُ رَبِّي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction; لولا is a particle of prevention due to existence; نعمة is a mubtadaʾ and ربي a muḍāf ilayhi; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is necessarily omitted, the estimate being "existing"; the lām occurs in the answer to لولا; كان and its noun; and من المحضرين is its khabar, i.e. of those who were brought to the punishment as you and the like of you were brought. (أَفَما نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ): The hamza is for interrogation; the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, the estimate being "Are we immortal and favoured? Then we are not dying"; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative; نحن is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and ميتين is genitive by the bāʾ in form, accusative in position as the khabar of ما. (إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا الْأُولى وَما نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ): إلا is a particle of restriction and the exception is emptied (mufarragh); موتتنا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; it is also said to be a discontinuous exception, so it is accusative as the excepted; الأولى is an adjective, i.e. the death that was in the world; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative; نحن its noun; and بمعذبين: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and معذبين is genitive in form, accusative in position as the khabar of ما. (إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): إن and its noun, the shifted lām; هو is a mubtadaʾ or a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); الفوز is the khabar of هو and the clause is the khabar of إن, or it is the khabar of إن; and العظيم is an adjective of الفوز.
(لِمِثْلِ هذا فَلْيَعْمَلِ الْعامِلُونَ): It may be part of his speech, to encourage the legally responsible to do acts of obedience, and it may be part of the speech of some of them to others. It is said that the second possibility is remote because of His saying «فليعمل العاملون», since action and encouragement to it occur only in the world. In any case, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يعمل; هذا is a muḍāf ilayhi; the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. "if the reality of the state of the people of Paradise has become clear, then let them act"; the lām is the lām of command; يعمل is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; and العاملون is the agent.

dervis-irab:114-122.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلى مُوسى وَهارُونَ) A resumptive passage introduced to begin the third story; you may also make the wāw a conjunction upon what preceded. The lām is the response to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; مننا is a verb and agent; and على موسى وهارون is attached to مننا, i.e. We favoured them with prophethood and other religious and worldly distinctions.
(وَنَجَّيْناهُما وَقَوْمَهُما مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ) The wāw is a conjunction; نجيناهما is conjoined to مننا, a verb, agent and direct object, the mīm and alif being two particles indicating the dual; قومهما is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the pronoun in نجيناهما; من الكرب is attached to نجيناهما; and العظيم is an adjective of الكرب, by which is meant Pharaoh's enslaving them and inflicting on them an evil punishment.
(وَنَصَرْناهُمْ فَكانُوا هُمُ الْغالِبِينَ) Conjoined to what preceded. The pronoun is plural because it refers to Moses, Aaron and their people. فكانوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; kāna and its noun; هم is a separation pronoun with no position; and الغالبين is the khabar of كانوا. Some allowed هم to be an emphasis (tawkīd) of the wāw or a substitute for it.
(وَآتَيْناهُمَا الْكِتابَ الْمُسْتَبِينَ) Also conjoined to what preceded. الكتاب is the second direct object and المستبين is an adjective of الكتاب, by which is meant the Torah and the legislation and rulings it contains.
(وَهَدَيْناهُمَا الصِّراطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ) Conjoined to what preceded; الصراط is a second direct object or accusative by removal of the preposition, as has preceded; and المستقيم is an adjective of الصراط.
(وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِما فِي الْآخِرِينَ) Its parsing has preceded more than once.
(سَلامٌ عَلى مُوسى وَهارُونَ) سلام is a mubtadaʾ and على موسى وهارون is its khabar.
(إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) inna and its noun; كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; and the clause نجزي المحسنين is the khabar of inna. Similar cases have preceded.
(إِنَّهُما مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) inna and its noun; من عبادنا is the khabar; and المؤمنين is an adjective.

* Benefits:
The truth about the word Mūsā (Moses):
The correct view is that Mūsā is a non-Arabic proper name, not derived. The saying of some that it is derived from awsaytu al-shajar, i.e. "I took the leaves off it", is weak. Ibn al-Sarrāj rejected all of this and said: whoever derives something from a non-Arabic language from the Arabic language is in the position of one who claims that the bird is the offspring of the fish. Although Mūsā is non-Arabic, there is disagreement about its pattern. Sībawayh said its pattern is mufʿal, which is also the view of Abū ʿAmr; al-Kisāʾī said its pattern is fuʿlā. The argument for Sībawayh is that the addition of the mīm at the beginning is more frequent than the addition of the alif at the end. Al-Fārisī answered al-Kisāʾī by its being fully declined (muṣraf) when indefinite; had it been fuʿlā, its alif would be for the feminine, and it would not be declined when indefinite either. Whoever allows the pattern fiʿlal among the forms, as al-Akhfash held, allows its alif to be for annexation (ilḥāq), so that it is declined when indefinite. And one says in its plural with wāw and nūn: mūsawna and mūsayna, with a fatḥa on the sīn, among the Basrans and the Kufans, if its pattern is mufʿal; and on al-Kisāʾī's way one says mūsūna, with a damma on the sīn before the wāw, and mūsīna, with a kasra on the sīn before the yāʾ. All this concerns Mūsā as the name of one of the children of Adam. As for al-mūsā with which hair is shaved (the razor), it is Arabic. It is then said to be derived from asawtu al-shayʾ when I mended it, the original being muʾsā with a hamza, and the hamza was changed to wāw; and it was said to be from awsaytu, I shaved, and this is better known, and on this its wāw has no origin in a hamza.
